title: Continuous frames identify coefficient sheaves and their scalar extension
statement:
Let $K$ be a field with a topology making its field operations continuous, and let $A\subseteq K$ be a subring with the subspace topology. Let $r\geq0$ and $L\subseteq K^r$ be an $A$-submodule, with the subspace topology from the product topology. Suppose $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in L$ are an $A$-basis of $L$ and a $K$-basis of $K^r$, and that $\beta:A^r\to L$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i b_i$, is a homeomorphism. Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a topological ring $T$, put $T_S(U)=C(|U|,T)$ with pointwise operations and precomposition restrictions, as in [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients]. Define $F_L(U)=C(|U|,L)$ with pointwise $A_S(U)$-action and the same restrictions. Then $A_S,K_S$ are sheaves of rings and $F_L$ is a sheaf of $A_S$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The maps
$$\phi_U:A_S(U)^r\xrightarrow{\sim}F_L(U),\qquad (a_i)\mapsto\bigl(x\mapsto\sum_i a_i(x)b_i\bigr),$$
with inverse $f\mapsto(x\mapsto(\beta^{-1}(f(x)))_i)_i$, are $A_S(U)$-linear isomorphisms commuting with every restriction. In particular $F_L\cong A_S^r$ as module sheaves. The actual inclusion $\iota:F_L\hookrightarrow K_S^r$ is postcomposition with $L\subseteq K^r$. For every $U$, its scalar-extension map
$$\mu_U:K_S(U)\otimes_{A_S(U)}F_L(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|U|,K^r),\qquad a\otimes f\mapsto\bigl(x\mapsto a(x)f(x)\bigr)$$
is a $K_S(U)$-linear isomorphism. If $B\in\operatorname{GL}_r(K)$ has columns $b_i$ and $\underline b_i$ denotes the constant $L$-valued section, its inverse sends $g$ to $\sum_i (B^{-1}g)_i\otimes\underline b_i$. The maps $\mu_U$ and their inverses commute with every restriction. Under $\phi_U$ and the identification $a\otimes(a_i)_i\mapsto(aa_i)_i$, the map $\mu_U$ is multiplication by the constant matrix $B$. Thus the presheaf tensor product is already a sheaf, and the morphism $K_S\otimes_{A_S}F_L\to K_S^r$ induced by $\iota$ is an isomorphism for the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. All assertions include $r=0$.
